These Terms of Service (“Terms”) govern all services provided by Hosting Nigeria (“we”, “us”, “our”) to customers (“you”, “your”). By purchasing, renewing, or using our services, you agree to these Terms and our applicable policies.

1. General Terms

Hosting Nigeria provides shared hosting, reseller hosting, VPS, dedicated servers, domain registration, website development, and related services.

We reserve the right to refuse, suspend, restrict, or terminate services where reasonably necessary due to non-payment, fraud, security threats, illegal activities, or violations of these Terms.

Customers must provide accurate registration information, maintain secure account credentials, and comply with applicable laws.

2. Customer Websites and Third-Party Liability

Hosting Nigeria operates as a hosting infrastructure provider and does not own, operate, supervise, endorse, or control websites, applications, businesses, or content hosted by customers.

Customers are solely responsible for their websites, applications, content, transactions, security, products, services, and interactions with their users.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, Hosting Nigeria shall not be liable for losses or damages suffered by website visitors, customers, or third parties arising from customer-controlled activities, including:

  • Fraud, scams, phishing, or financial losses.

  • Identity theft, data theft, or privacy violations.

  • Malware, harmful content, or security breaches.

  • Failed transactions, undelivered products, or misleading advertisements.

  • Copyright infringement or other unlawful activities.

  • Any other harm arising from a customer’s website, application, business, or conduct.

Hosting Nigeria is not a party to transactions between customers and their website users merely because those transactions occur through our infrastructure.

Providing hosting services does not constitute endorsement or verification of a customer’s business.

Customers agree to indemnify and hold Hosting Nigeria, its directors, employees, and representatives harmless against qualifying third-party claims, damages, and reasonable legal expenses arising from their unlawful activities, content, or contractual breaches, except to the extent caused by Hosting Nigeria’s own legally actionable conduct.

Nothing in this section excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

3. Uptime and Service Availability

Hosting Nigeria targets 99.95% monthly uptime for eligible hosting services, excluding scheduled maintenance, customer-caused issues, cyberattacks, third-party network failures, force majeure events, and circumstances outside our reasonable control.

We do not guarantee uninterrupted or error-free service.

Where applicable, service credits shall be governed by the relevant Service Level Agreement. No automatic financial compensation is payable for downtime unless required by law or expressly agreed.

We may conduct emergency maintenance without prior notice where necessary to protect our infrastructure.

4. Payments, Renewals, and Termination

All services are payable in advance and must be renewed before expiry.

Unpaid services may be suspended immediately upon expiry. Standard termination timelines are:

  • Shared and Reseller Hosting: 21 days after expiry.

  • VPS and Dedicated Servers: 24 hours after expiry.

  • Other Services: Within 24 hours after expiry, where applicable.

These periods do not guarantee continued access after expiry.

Hosting Nigeria may terminate services earlier following serious abuse, security threats, fraud, or a valid cancellation request.

Terminated services may have their files, databases, emails, backups, and configurations permanently deleted without further notice, subject to applicable law.

Customers are responsible for backing up their data before expiry or cancellation.

Restoration after termination is not guaranteed. Where possible, a ₦5,000 reactivation fee may apply alongside outstanding charges.

Failure to receive renewal reminders does not excuse late payment.

Hosting Nigeria may change prices for future billing periods, subject to applicable notice requirements.

5. Refunds and Chargebacks

Payments for successfully provisioned services are generally non-refundable, including hosting setup, domain registrations, VPS provisioning, SSL certificates, and completed website development work.

Refunds may be issued for duplicate payments, overpayments, failed transactions, or services we cannot provide.

Early cancellation does not automatically entitle customers to prorated refunds.

Hosting Nigeria may suspend services associated with fraudulent payments, reversed transactions, or chargebacks while the matter is investigated.

Customers remain responsible for valid outstanding balances and lawfully recoverable charges.

Nothing in this section limits mandatory statutory refund or consumer rights.

6. Acceptable Use and Security

Customers must use our services lawfully. Prohibited activities include:

  • Phishing, fraud, scams, and impersonation.

  • Malware, hacking, botnets, and DDoS attacks.

  • Spam and unauthorised bulk email.

  • Child exploitation material and other illegal content.

  • Copyright infringement and software piracy.

  • Illegal gambling, drug trafficking, and other unlawful businesses.

  • Cryptocurrency mining or unauthorised proxy services.

  • Activities that threaten server security, performance, or other customers.

Hosting Nigeria may immediately suspend, isolate, restrict, or terminate accounts involved in serious abuse or presenting credible security threats, without prior notice where reasonably necessary.

Customers are responsible for keeping their websites, software, plugins, passwords, and applications secure.

We may investigate abuse complaints, preserve relevant records, and cooperate with competent authorities where legally permitted or required.

7. Resource Usage and Reseller Responsibilities

Customers must comply with the CPU, RAM, storage, bandwidth, inode, email, and other limits applicable to their plans.

Any advertised unlimited resources remain subject to fair usage and technical restrictions.

Hosting Nigeria may restrict resource-intensive activities or suspend services that threaten server stability.

Resellers are responsible for their customers, hosting accounts, content, support arrangements, and compliance with these Terms.

Hosting Nigeria may suspend individual reseller accounts or an entire reseller service where reasonably necessary to address serious violations.

Resellers shall be responsible for qualifying third-party claims arising from their own or their end users’ wrongful activities, subject to applicable law.

8. Backups and Data Loss

Customers are responsible for maintaining independent, up-to-date backups of their websites, emails, databases, and other information.

Any backup services provided by Hosting Nigeria are subject to the features of the purchased plan.

Unless expressly guaranteed in writing, Hosting Nigeria does not guarantee backup availability, completeness, retention, or successful restoration.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, Hosting Nigeria shall not be liable for data loss caused by customer errors, compromised accounts, expired services, third-party failures, or circumstances outside our reasonable control.

Customers must download necessary data before requesting cancellation or allowing services to expire.

9. Domain Registration and Transfers

Domain registrations, renewals, and transfers are subject to applicable registry, registrar, and ICANN policies.

Customers are responsible for providing accurate registration details and renewing domains before expiry.

Hosting Nigeria does not guarantee the availability, successful registration, renewal, transfer, or recovery of any domain.

Expired domains may attract redemption or restoration fees and may become permanently unavailable.

Applicable 60-day transfer restrictions shall follow relevant registry and ICANN rules.

Domain registration fees are generally non-refundable once registration is completed, subject to applicable law.

10. Third-Party Providers and Infrastructure

Hosting Nigeria relies on third-party data centres, network operators, registrars, software providers, and payment processors.

We shall not be liable for failures attributable solely to third parties outside our reasonable control, except where applicable law provides otherwise.

We may change infrastructure providers, server locations, IP allocations, or technical configurations where reasonably necessary for operational, security, or service delivery purposes.

Customers using unmanaged VPS or dedicated servers are responsible for their own operating systems, software, configurations, security, and maintenance.

11. Technical Support and Migrations

Hosting Nigeria provides technical support through its official channels, including tickets, email, live chat, and telephone where available.

Support availability does not guarantee immediate resolution.

Support does not automatically include custom programming, website redesign, application debugging, malware removal, or third-party software maintenance.

Courtesy website migrations may be provided within the first 30 days of eligible hosting purchases.

Migration success, compatibility, and completion times are not guaranteed. Customers must maintain backups and verify migrated services.

12. Privacy and Customer Information

Hosting Nigeria processes customer information in accordance with applicable data protection laws and its Privacy Policy.

Information may be disclosed to authorised service providers, payment processors, registrars, professional advisers, or competent authorities where legally permitted or required.

Customers are responsible for complying with applicable privacy and data protection requirements concerning information collected through their own websites and applications.

Hosting Nigeria may retain necessary account, billing, security, and transaction records for legitimate operational and legal purposes.

13. Limitation of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, Hosting Nigeria shall not be liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential losses, including lost profits, business interruption, lost revenue, reputational damage, or lost business opportunities.

Our total aggregate liability arising from a particular service shall not exceed the fees actually paid for that affected service during the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, to the extent such limitation is legally enforceable.

Hosting Nigeria shall not be responsible for losses attributable solely to customer negligence, customer-controlled software, unlawful customer activities, compromised customer credentials, or events outside our reasonable control.

Nothing in these Terms excludes liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, or other liabilities that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.

14. Customer Indemnification

Customers agree, to the maximum extent permitted by law, to indemnify and defend Hosting Nigeria, its directors, employees, and authorised representatives against qualifying third-party claims, liabilities, damages, and reasonable legal expenses arising from:

  • Fraudulent or unlawful customer activities.

  • Harmful websites, applications, or content controlled by customers.

  • Customer infringement of intellectual property or privacy rights.

  • Customer security failures or negligent operations.

  • Material violations of these Terms.

  • Wrongful activities carried out through reseller-controlled accounts.

This obligation applies to the extent the relevant loss is legally attributable to the customer and does not cover Hosting Nigeria’s own unlawful conduct.

Indemnification obligations survive termination of the hosting agreement.

15. Changes, Cancellation, and Disputes

Customers may request cancellation through their client dashboard or an approved verified support channel.

Hosting Nigeria may modify these Terms, service specifications, or pricing, subject to applicable notice requirements. Material changes shall take effect on the stated effective date.

These Terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Disputes should first be submitted through our official support channels for resolution. Unresolved disputes may be brought before courts of competent jurisdiction in Nigeria, subject to applicable law.

If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in effect.

Failure by Hosting Nigeria to enforce any provision does not constitute a waiver of its rights.

Provisions concerning outstanding payments, liability, indemnification, and dispute resolution survive termination.

16. Acceptance of Terms

By purchasing, renewing, or using Hosting Nigeria’s services after being presented with these Terms, customers acknowledge their acceptance of the applicable contractual conditions.

Customers confirm that they have had an opportunity to review the provisions concerning payments, refunds, service suspension, permanent data deletion, customer responsibilities, indemnification, and limitations of liability.
